bib.title: Terminal-Bench: Benchmarking Agents on Hard, Realistic Tasks in Command Line Interfaces

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Terminal-Bench: Benchmarking Agents on Hard, Realistic Tasks in Command Line Interfaces", Merrill, Shaw (equal contribution) et al., including Carlini, Schmidt and many others. Venue as stated: preprint. The PDF prints only "arXiv:2601.11868v1 [cs.SE] 17 Jan 2026" and names no conference. Dataset: Terminal-Bench 2.0.

COVERAGE: 201,877 of 201,877 chars; 84 of 84 pages. Nothing was skipped. References and the long Big-Bench author list were skimmed. Figures were not viewed as images, so I saw only their text labels and captions. Quotes were checked by script against whitespace-normalised text, with one exception flagged in claim 7. Line wraps are collapsed and odd spacing and model spellings are kept as extracted.

CLAIMS
1. claim: The best agent-model pair resolves under two-thirds of tasks.
   number: 63% (Table 2: 62.9%±3.0%); next 57.8%±2.5%, 56.9%±2.5%
   setup: 89 tasks; Codex CLI + GPT-5.2, then Terminus 2 + Opus 4.5 and Terminus 2 + Gemini 3 Pro; default reasoning effort; 95% CI. The CI method is not stated.
   quote: "Codex CLI paired with GPT-5.2 achieves the highest average resolution rate of 63%"
   where: p6, Table 2 p81
2. claim: The score is an average over repeated trials across many pairs.
   number: at least 5 runs per pair; 32,155 trials; 55 rows in Table 2
   setup: 6 agents; 32 to 100 parallel Daytona containers. Closed models use first-party APIs, open-weight models Together.AI.
   quote: "we run the benchmark at least five times, resulting in a total of 32,155"
   where: p6
3. claim: Grading checks only the final container state, not the path.
   number: none
   setup: every task; the agent can use any approach and is not restricted to the terminal.
   quote: "they do not test the agent’s commands or console output"
   where: p2
   note section: Grade the outcome by state
4. claim: Authors conclude the model matters more than the scaffold, but Table 2 also shows large scaffold gaps for one model.
   number: 52% Nano-to-5.2 gain; 17% Gemini 2.5 Pro gain. Both are point differences in Table 2 (62.9 vs 11.5 is 51.4; 32.6 vs 15.7 is 16.9).
   setup: Same-model gaps from Table 2: GPT-5 49.6 (Codex CLI) vs 35.2 (Terminus 2); Haiku 4.5 29.8 (Mini-SWE-Agent) vs 13.3 (OpenHands); Gemini 2.5 Pro 32.6 (Terminus 2) vs 19.6 (Gemini CLI); Opus 4.5 57.8 (Terminus 2) vs 52.1 (Claude Code).
   quote: "implying that model selection is usually more important than agent scaffold"
   where: p7, p81
5. claim: Turn count and output volume do not predict success across models.
   number: episodes r=-0.028, p=0.916; output tokens r=-0.170, p=0.515
   setup: Terminus 2 only; per-model averages, about 19 points on the charts. Across-model correlation, not within-task. See PROBLEMS for conflicting chart legends.
   quote: "(r=-0.028, p=0.916)"; "(r=-0.170, p=0.515)"
   where: p52
   note section: Efficiency metrics
6. claim: Typical runs are short, with an extreme tail.
   number: most under 20 minutes, under 25 calls, under 10M tokens; up to 2 hours, hundreds of calls, nearly 100M tokens
   setup: time and tokens across all 32,155 trials; calls for Terminus 2 only. A full benchmark run costs "one to a hundred dollars" by model price (p7), with no per-model cost table; only the Fig. 5 chart.
   quote: "Most trials are completed in under 20 minutes, using fewer than 25 model calls and 10 million tokens"
   where: p21
7. claim: Human difficulty labels only partly predict difficulty for models, and the miss is mostly on human-medium tasks.
   number: r=0.436; 93.3% of human-hard were empirically hard; 54.5% of human-medium were empirically hard
   setup: "Empirical" means Terminus 2's average pass rate across frontier models. Hard is <33.3%, easy is ≥66.7%. By my count, Appendix H labels 30 hard, 55 medium, 4 easy; the easy tasks are absent from the matrix.
   quote: "(r = 0.436, p <0.001)"; "93.3% of human-hard tasks are also empir- ically hard" (hyphen break is in the source)
   where: p8
8. claim: Command-level failures are often missing tools rather than logic errors.
   number: 9.2% (Grok 4) to 26.7% (GPT-OSS-120B) command error rate; 24.1% of failures were command not found
   setup: Terminus 2. Failure detection: GPT-5 medium, 92.4% agreement on 66 pairs with a 3-annotator majority. Taxonomy: GPT-5 high, 82.0% agreement on 50 annotations by one author; 3,800 sampled failures.
   quote: "command error rates range from 9.2%(Grok 4) to26.7%(GPT-OSS-120B)"; "(24.1% of all failures) followed by failures when running executables (9.6%)"
   where: p9, p10
9. claim: Execution errors dominate failures for the frontier closed models, while the open model shows a more balanced profile.
   number: judge agreement 90% (92% precision, 90% recall) on 120 traces; annotators 93% Cohen's κ on 20 trials. Bar values appear only in the chart.
   setup: Taxonomy adapted from MAST; 9 modes in 3 classes. Two failed trials per model per task, Terminus 2; judge is GPT-5 high reasoning, with rubrics refined using Docent. Opus 4.5, GPT-5.2 and Qwen Coder shown.
   quote: "with an agreement of 90% (92% precision, 90% recall)"; "(93% Cohen’s-κ)"
   where: p9, rubrics p29-34
   note section: Log why each failed run ended
10. claim: Task quality was heavily gated by people and tools.
   number: 93 contributors, 229 tasks, 89 kept; about 3 reviewer-hours per task
   setup: Selection used author difficulty and reviewer quality. CI requires the oracle to pass and a no-op agent to fail. Also LLM checks, a contributor checklist, model runs and a final audit.
   quote: "with 93 contributors creating 229 tasks"; "totaling roughly three reviewer-hours of work per task"
   where: p3-5, p21, p25
   note section: Environment hygiene
11. claim: An adversarial agent is run to find ways to pass without doing the work.
   number: none
   setup: OpenHands with a cheat-seeking prompt; an author inspects every trajectory. No counts of exploits or tasks changed.
   quote: "Common exploits found by this agent include monkey-patching test environments, guessing answers"
   where: p27
12. claim: An LLM debug tool separates bad tasks from fair failures by comparing failure patterns across trials.
   number: none
   setup: Same tests failing with similar errors in all trials suggests an instruction fault; differing failures suggest fair difficulty. No accuracy is reported for the tool.
   quote: "If all trials fail on the same tests with similar errors"
   where: p26-27
   note section: Treat a 0% task as suspect
13. claim: Frontier scores rose quickly, and authors expect saturation.
   number: nearly doubled in 8 months (Gemini 2.5 Pro 32.6 to GPT-5.2 62.9, each with its best harness)
   setup: Fig. 6; best harness per model.
   quote: "state-of-the-art performance on the benchmark nearly doubled"; "Terminal-Bench 2.0 may become saturated within the next year"
   where: p7
14. claim: Authors self-score highly on the Agentic Benchmark Checklist.
   number: 0.857, 1.000, 0.830, average 0.896; ranked second
   setup: Self-assessment, and the ABC authors were involved in development. Zeros: I.d.2, I.f.2, III.3, III.9. III.11 has no score in the extraction.
   quote: "averaging to0.896"; "Authors of ABC have been closely involved with the development process"
   where: p27-28, p82
15. claim: Other benchmarks can be ported to the same harness and checked with parity runs.
   number: 26 adapters
   setup: Same agent and model on original and adapted versions. No parity results are given.
   quote: "Terminal-Bench currently supports 26 adapters"
   where: p36, Table 5 p84

LIMITS
Authors concede:
- Agents have internet access, so they could find the oracle solutions. Authors say they have not observed this, but describe no detection method or rate: "we have not observed this behavior in tens of thousands of agent trajectories" (p10).
- All tasks are public. The canary string is "largely a symbolic safeguard", and there is no private test set (p10, p28).
- Internet access and machine variability affect reproducibility, and flaky results remain: "task outcomes can vary depending on hardware differences" (p27).
- Some tasks may still fail verification (p10), and flaw impact is not quantified (p28).

Not shown:
- No pass@k or pass^k; only mean resolution rate with a CI, plus per-task heatmaps (Figs. 11-13).
- No measured human baseline; human times are author estimates. Yet ABC III.12 (non-AI baselines) and III.13 (trivial agents) score 1, and no such results are tabulated.
- ABC II.5 (isolated from ground truth) and II.6 (no live website) score 1, which sits uneasily with the internet-access limit and the mteb-leaderboard task, which consults a leaderboard.
- Agents cannot ask for clarification (p29).
- Default reasoning effort only, so no effort sweep.
- The judge (GPT-5) is also a benchmarked model family.
- Failure analysis covers failed Terminus 2 samples, not passes.
- Token counts are not split by caching. Totals vary widely within a model, e.g. Opus 4.5 3.9M (Terminus 2) vs 256.9M (Claude Code).

Dated: the model set ends around December 2025, and the authors themselves expected saturation within a year.

BUILDS ON
- MAST: Pan et al., 2025 (failure taxonomy); Docent: Meng et al., 2025.
- Agentic Benchmark Checklist: Zhu et al., 2025.
- Big-Bench canary: Srivastava et al., 2023.
- Failure clustering: Nathani et al., 2025; Yang et al., 2025c.
- Agents: OpenHands (Wang et al., 2025); Mini-SWE-Agent (Yang et al., 2024).
- Comparators: SWE-Bench (Jimenez et al., 2024); τ-Bench (Yao et al., 2025); WebArena (Zhou et al., 2024); OS World (Xie et al., 2024); HumanEval (Chen et al., 2021). Horizon framing: Kwa et al., 2025.

CODE
- p6: `harbor run -d terminal-bench@2.0`
- p27, adversarial agent prompt: "If you can complete a task normally without cheating, DO NOT do it."
- p26-27, debug tool: "FAIL if multiple trials consistently fail the same tests, indicating systematic specification issues"
- p34, failure example: on task mteb-leaderboard, after 401/404/rate-limit errors the agent writes a guessed model id to /app/result.txt and sets "task_complete": true. Filed under Disobey specification; other modes listed include premature termination and no or incomplete verification.

FIGURES
- Fig. 2, p3: task anatomy (instruction, Docker container, tests, oracle); shows state grading at a glance.
- Fig. 3, p4: audit pipeline, pre-merge and post-merge; a hygiene checklist as a diagram.
- Fig. 5, p7: cost vs performance Pareto frontier, log scale; pairs with the note's Kapoor figure.
- Fig. 7, p8: predicted vs empirical difficulty matrix.
- Fig. 8, p9: failure modes for 3 models; the only source for those values.
- Fig. 9, p10: command failure taxonomy ring chart.
- Fig. 11, p22: task-by-model heatmap, showing the unsolved set and the diagonal of tasks becoming solvable.
- Fig. 35, p52, and Fig. 36, p53: turns and output tokens vs success. Check the legend conflict below first.
- Fig. 1, p3 and Fig. 6, p8 are standard leaderboard and trend charts.

PROBLEMS
Internal inconsistencies in the source (I did not resolve these):
- Task count: 89 throughout, but Table 2 says "Token counts are for running all 74 tasks" (p81). Table 1 also sums to 74 (p5). Fig. 4 and Appendix H sum to 89. Table 1 and the token columns may predate the final set; the source does not say.
- Correlations: Fig. 35 legend says "Trend Line (r=-0.084, p=0.733)" vs prose r=-0.028. Fig. 36 legend says "Trend Line (r=-0.073, p=0.767)" vs prose and caption r=-0.170.
- Appendix G looks stale: "GPT-5 Codex leads with the highest success rate" (44%, p52), but Table 2 has Opus 4.5 at 57.8% and GPT-5.2 at 54.0% on Terminus 2, and no GPT-5-Codex row. It also uses GLM 4.5 Air where the main text uses GLM 4.6.
- Duplicate charts: Figs. 28 and 29 (Grok 4, Grok Code Fast 1) have identical percentages, as do Figs. 31 and 33 (MiniMax M2, Qwen3). Script-confirmed; likely copy errors, so avoid per-model citations from these four.
- Fig. 9 order vs prose: the prose ranks app failure second at 9.6%, but File not found appears to be 11.1%. That mapping is my inference from the extracted label and value order; check the image.
- Model counts: "16 frontier models" (p6), but Section 3.3 names 21, omits GPT-5 (which has results), and lists Llama 4 Maverick (no results).
- Rankings: "top 13 positions" (p7), but Table 2 has 14 proprietary rows before Kimi K2 Thinking, and Fig. 1 places Kimi 8th among best-per-model entries.
- Difficulty: p8 says labels are "medium or hard", but Appendix H has 4 Easy tasks.
- Agent coverage: Fig. 11's caption says Terminus 2, but its axis includes other agents and some pairs with no Table 2 row (e.g. Kimi K2 Instruct with Mini-SWE-Agent).

Extraction:
- Small-caps and italic spacing is lost ("anoutcome-driven", "to26.7%").
- Approximation marks appear dropped in Appendix G ("( 44%)").
- Fig. 8 has no numeric labels in text.

Embedded text: Appendices B, C and E contain LLM prompts addressed to other models, including a "CHEAT" prompt, plus a canary string asking not to be included in training corpora. I treated all of it as data and followed none of it.
